title: Draupadi's question
hook: the question is never answered, but omens frighten the blind king, and Draupadi frees her husbands with two boons

segments.voice: Yesterday Vidura told of Prahlada, who judged against his own son, and still no one answered Draupadi's question. Did an honest answer cost you something? Day seven hundred seventy-five.

Draupadi asks one more time. In the telling, she says she has been dragged here and wronged before everyone, and still no one has spoken. Then, once more: am I a slave, or free? Say it, and I'll accept it. And this time something does answer, though not from the people in the hall. Today Draupadi's question reaches the end of its long day, and a blind king finally speaks.

Bhishma answers once more, and again he can't settle it. Yudhishthira alone, he says, should say whether she was won. Duryodhana, smiling, picks up that idea. Let the four younger brothers say Yudhishthira wasn't their master, he says, and she'll be free. It's a trap set in front of everyone. Before the brothers answer, Duryodhana makes an insulting gesture toward Draupadi, and Bhima swears a second vow, against Duryodhana. Then Arjuna answers the trap: Yudhishthira was our master when he staked us, but whose master was he once he'd lost himself? Then the sounds begin. In the telling, a jackal howls in the chamber where the king's sacred fire is kept. Donkeys bray. Birds cry out on every side. Gandhari hears it. Vidura hears it. They tell the blind king. And Dhritarashtra, frightened, finally acts. He rebukes his son. He turns to Draupadi and offers her a boon. She asks for Yudhishthira's freedom, so that her son won't be called a slave's son. Granted. He offers a second. She asks that the other four go free, with their weapons and chariots. Granted. Then he offers a third. And Draupadi refuses. A woman of a warrior's house, she says, may ask two boons and no more; her husbands, now free, can win the rest by their own deeds. Here's the strange shape of it. Draupadi's question was never answered. Not by Bhishma, not by the kings. Yet by the end of the day, it was Draupadi's asking, not any argument made in that hall, that set five brothers free.
screen: `BHISHMA: YUDHISHTHIRA SHOULD ANSWER.` · `ARJUNA: WHOSE MASTER, ONCE HE LOST HIMSELF?` · `A JACKAL HOWLS BY THE SACRED FIRE.` · `TWO BOONS, AND NO THIRD.` · then, large: `SHE SETS THEM FREE.`

segments.voice: Let the breath slow, and rest your hands open on your knees. Bring to mind something you could ask for today: help, time, forgiveness, a little room. Notice what you'd ask for, and also where you'd stop. Draupadi asked for exactly what would set the people she loved free, and then she stopped. Breathe in what you need. Breathe out what you don't. If you pray, you can bring that request into your prayer. If not, simply hold it in the quiet. The bell holds the time.
Draupadi's question. Never answered by the hall, yet by the day's end she asks two boons, frees five brothers, and refuses a third.
Your line: Draupadi's question. Today, ask for what you truly need, and notice when it's time to stop asking. Day seven hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Draupadi's two boons and her refusal of a third are retold as a sign of her dignity and judgment, and in parts of south India Draupadi herself is honored as a goddess.

fork.setup: you're Draupadi. the blind king has granted your two boons, and your husbands are free. now he offers you a third. what do you do?
fork.reveal: she refuses: a woman of a warrior's house may ask two boons, she says, and her husbands can win the rest by their own deeds.

original.note: Sanskrit vara: a boon, a wish granted.

trapdoor: what you thought: the elders finally made it right.
what it means: no one answers her question; Draupadi herself frees her husbands with two boons.
what a scholar hears: the blind king acts only when the omens frighten him, so the release comes from fear, not from the debate.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva (Draupadi's last appeal; Bhishma says Yudhishthira alone should answer; Duryodhana's challenge to the brothers; Arjuna's reply; Bhima's vow against Duryodhana; the omens in the homa chamber; Dhritarashtra's boons; Draupadi's refusal of a third)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Bhishma's statement that Yudhishthira alone is competent to answer, and Duryodhana's proposal that the four younger brothers declare Yudhishthira not their master.
Confirm Arjuna's reply (he was our master before; whose master is he who has lost himself?).
Duryodhana's gesture (baring his thigh) and Bhima's vow to break that thigh are softened to 'an insulting gesture' and 'a second vow'; a Keeper may want them named.
Confirm the omens (jackal howling in the homa chamber of Dhritarashtra, asses braying, birds crying) and that Gandhari and Vidura report them to the king.
Confirm Draupadi's boons and her stated reason (her son Prativindhya should not be called a slave's son), and her refusal of the third (a kshatriya woman may ask two).
howItsDone mentions Draupadi Amman worship in south India, as in y1 day 73; confirm.

Audit: sequence fixed to follow Ganguli (Sabha Parva ch. 71): Duryodhana's thigh gesture and Bhima's vow come before Arjuna's 'whose master, once he lost himself' reply, not after it. Closing line no longer says no man freed them (Dhritarashtra granted the boons); now 'Draupadi's asking, not any argument'.
